front: The lesson splits environmental risk factors into three groups. What are they?
answer: Weather conditions / Playing surfaces / Human interaction
title: Extrinsic Factors

front: The lesson splits sports equipment into three categories. What are they?
answer: Protective equipment / Performance equipment / Clothing and footwear
title: Extrinsic Factors

front: Why can poor officiating increase the risk of injury during a match?
answer: Officials enforce the rules and control the game, so poor officiating lets dangerous play continue unchecked.
title: Extrinsic Factors

front: Why can spectators encroaching onto the pitch increase the risk of injury to performers?
answer: They can distract performers or collide with them, causing injuries during play.
title: Extrinsic Factors

front: The lesson splits intrinsic factors into four areas. What are they?
answer: Individual variables / Psychological factors / Reasons for aggression / Mental strategies
title: Intrinsic Factors

front: The lesson gives five reasons why aggression happens in sport. What are they?
answer: Level of performance / Retaliation / Pressure to win / Decisions of officials / Performance-enhancing drugs
title: Intrinsic Factors

front: Why does fatigue increase a performer's risk of injury?
answer: Fatigued muscles cannot support the body properly, making injuries more likely.
title: Intrinsic Factors

front: Why can returning to sport too soon after an injury cause a new injury elsewhere in the body?
answer: The performer may unconsciously alter their movement patterns to protect the healing area, causing problems elsewhere.
title: Intrinsic Factors

front: The lesson gives six physiological benefits of warming up. What are they?
items: Increase in pliability of ligaments and tendons
Increase in blood flow and oxygen delivery
Increase in speed of muscle contraction
answer: Increase in muscle temperature / Increase in heart rate / Increase in flexibility / Increase in pliability of ligaments and tendons / Increase in blood flow and oxygen delivery / Increase in speed of muscle contraction
title: Warm Up Routines

front: The lesson gives four psychological benefits of warming up. What are they?
answer: Increased focus and concentration / Opportunity for mental rehearsal / Reduced anxiety / Increased confidence
title: Warm Up Routines

front: How do mobility exercises like arm swings and hip circles reduce injury risk?
answer: They increase the pliability of ligaments and tendons, letting joints move further during activity without damage.
title: Warm Up Routines

front: Why are warm muscles less likely to tear than cold muscles?
answer: Warm muscles release energy more readily and become more flexible, making them less likely to tear.
title: Warm Up Routines

front: The lesson gives three stages of a cool down. What are they?
answer: Pulse lowering / Static stretching / Deep breathing and relaxation
title: Cool Down Routines

front: The lesson gives four consequences of skipping a cool down. What are they?
items: Increased muscle stiffness and reduced flexibility
answer: DOMS / Blood pooling / Increased muscle stiffness and reduced flexibility / Slower recovery time
title: Cool Down Routines

front: Why must exercise intensity reduce gradually at the end of a session rather than stop suddenly?
answer: A gradual reduction keeps blood circulating to the brain instead of pooling in the arms and legs.
title: Cool Down Routines

front: Why does DOMS tend to be worse if you skip the cool down?
answer: Without a cool down keeping blood flowing to the muscle fibres, they cannot recover as well.
title: Cool Down Routines

front: The lesson names three types of fracture. What are they?
answer: Simple (closed) fracture / Compound (open) fracture / Stress fracture
title: Acute Sports Injuries

front: The lesson names four types of skin damage that count as acute soft tissue injuries. What are they?
answer: Abrasion (graze) / Laceration (cut) / Blister / Contusion (bruise)
title: Acute Sports Injuries

front: Why is a compound fracture more serious than a simple fracture?
answer: The bone breaks through the skin, creating an open wound with a much higher risk of infection.
title: Acute Sports Injuries

front: Why must players follow the Graduated Return to Play protocol after a concussion?
answer: Returning to play too soon risks a second head injury that could be even more dangerous.
title: Acute Sports Injuries

front: The lesson gives four ways to help prevent shin splints. What are they?
items: Strength training for the lower legs
answer: Appropriate running shoes with cushioning / Regular stretching / Strength training for the lower legs / Gradually increasing training intensity
title: Chronic Sports Injuries

front: The lesson names three types of tendonitis. What are they?
answer: Achilles tendonitis / Patellar tendonitis / Rotator cuff tendonitis
title: Chronic Sports Injuries

front: Why do jumping sports like basketball and volleyball cause patellar tendonitis?
answer: Repeated jumping and landing puts constant stress on the patellar tendon, causing pain and swelling.
title: Chronic Sports Injuries

front: How does repeated impact from overtraining cause a stress fracture?
answer: Repeated shock causes tiny cracks in the bone that worsen over time without rest.
title: Chronic Sports Injuries

front: The lesson names the three sections of an Emergency Action Plan. What are they?
answer: Emergency Personnel / Emergency Communication / Emergency Equipment
title: Reducing Risk & Emergency Action Plans

front: The lesson gives five characteristics to consider when assessing risk for an individual or group. What are they?
answer: Age / Individual fitness levels / Experience / Medical conditions / Group size
title: Reducing Risk & Emergency Action Plans

front: Why is CRY screening important for young athletes?
answer: It can detect hidden heart conditions that could be life-threatening during intense exercise.
title: Reducing Risk & Emergency Action Plans

front: Why can a large group on a pitch increase the risk of injury?
answer: Large groups increase the chance of collisions, make instructions harder to hear and reduce supervision per player.
title: Reducing Risk & Emergency Action Plans

front: The lesson gives the five steps of the DRABC protocol in order. What are they?
answer: Danger / Response / Airway / Breathing / Circulation
title: Treatment & Rehabilitation

front: The lesson gives the five steps of the PRICE protocol. What are they?
answer: Protection / Rest / Ice / Compression / Elevation
title: Treatment & Rehabilitation

front: Why does raising an injured limb above the heart reduce swelling?
answer: Gravity helps drain excess fluid away from the injury, reducing the swelling.
title: Treatment & Rehabilitation

front: Why is a graduated, supervised return to sport safer than rushing back after an injury?
answer: Rushing back risks the injury recurring, becoming chronic, or ending up worse than the original injury.
title: Treatment & Rehabilitation

front: The lesson gives four things you must NOT do during an epileptic seizure. What are they?
items: Try to move them (unless in danger)
Give them food or drink until fully recovered
answer: Restrain them / Put anything in their mouth / Try to move them (unless in danger) / Give them food or drink until fully recovered
title: Medical Conditions: Asthma, Diabetes & Epilepsy

front: The lesson gives six symptoms shared by both types of diabetes. What are they?
items: Cuts and wounds slow to heal
answer: Increased thirst / Frequent urination / Extreme tiredness / Unexplained weight loss / Cuts and wounds slow to heal / Blurred vision
title: Medical Conditions: Asthma, Diabetes & Epilepsy

front: Why does glucose build up in the blood in Type 1 diabetes?
answer: The body cannot make insulin, so glucose cannot enter the body's cells from the blood.
title: Medical Conditions: Asthma, Diabetes & Epilepsy

front: Why can Type 2 diabetes often be prevented while Type 1 cannot?
answer: Type 1 is an autoimmune condition, but Type 2 is strongly linked to lifestyle factors that can be changed.
title: Medical Conditions: Asthma, Diabetes & Epilepsy

front: The lesson gives three causes of sudden cardiac arrest in sport. What are they?
items: Sudden trauma to the chest (commotio cordis)
answer: Underlying genetic heart condition / Intense physical activity / Sudden trauma to the chest (commotio cordis)
title: Medical Conditions: SCA, Hypothermia, Heat Exhaustion & Dehydration

front: The lesson gives six symptoms of hypothermia. What are they?
answer: Shivering / Blue lips and skin / Slurred speech / Tiredness and confusion / Slow breathing / Loss of coordination
title: Medical Conditions: SCA, Hypothermia, Heat Exhaustion & Dehydration

front: How does an AED help restore a normal heart rhythm during cardiac arrest?
answer: It analyses the heart's rhythm and delivers a controlled shock that stops the chaotic activity, letting the heart reset.
title: Medical Conditions: SCA, Hypothermia, Heat Exhaustion & Dehydration

front: Why does high humidity make heat exhaustion more likely during exercise?
answer: High humidity makes it harder for sweat to evaporate, so the body struggles to cool itself.
title: Medical Conditions: SCA, Hypothermia, Heat Exhaustion & Dehydration
